title: malus sieversii subsp. hissarica
intro: Malus sieversii subsp. hissarica, commonly known as the Hissar crabapple, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the rose family Rosaceae. It is a wild apple species native to the mountainous regions of Central Asia, and its bark and leaves have been used in traditional medicine for centuries. The health benefits of Malus sieversii subsp. hissarica include its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which may help to reduce pain, fever, and inflammation. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and triterpenoids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, including cardiotonic, diaphoretic, and expectorant properties.
